newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bearish sentiment clouds SIMEX Nikkei, ends down.
newsitem.headline: Bearish sentiment clouds SIMEX Nikkei, ends down.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended weaker on Friday as bearish sentiment over the state of Japan's banking sector threatened to push the market even lower next week, dealers said.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) comments in its first quarter 1997 quarterly report that it was closely watching the impact of the stock market's fall on corporate sentiment fuelled caution over Japan's economy.
Dealers said the comment reinforced worries that corporate sentiment was very bearish, triggering the BOJ to postpone its February tankan to early April.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 290 points down at 17,660. Volume was moderate, around 14,565 lots.
The March contract hit a low of 17,510 in the morning on reports Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party was wavering in its plans to abolish the security transaction tax.
"The Nikkei should be coming down next week," said a chartist. "The support looks very weak, with all the oscillators pointing down."
The 18,180 level was seen as the first level resistance, which if broken, could see March heading higher towards 19,300.
However, most dealers felt the contract would head south to test supports at 16,950-16,960.
The SIMEX Taiwan March futures shaved off 0.2 points to end at 310.3 on 298 lots.
